Consider the square $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1\}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=u+v+1,\,y=u-v.
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u+v+1 \\ u-v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14273134/assets/0765c97ee895f6ba1c5d247076a685fdfa08ce11e1a03e4962b5d8d398f944ff.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(1,0),(2,1),(3,0),$ and $(2,-1).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14273134/assets/ba786b34d6e52836861492fb831bb996404668fb75c5fe9a17531058f0128de0.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-2<0,$ this transformation is orientation reversing.
